summary:
The design is sound in its main choices. The surrogate-bit classifier, keeping cut criteria 2 and 3 untouched, the P/Invoke volume read, the hidden-entry-safe EnumerationOptions reference and the TokenElevation check all hold up. MS-FSCC confirms the N bit means "represents another named entity". There are three major problems, all at the volume-figure seam.

(M1) The claim that a stalled read cannot pin the store is enforced only inside VolumeSpace.cs. The App consumer is left as "whatever blocking structure it has now". Its wait or await sits on the same TaskCompletionSource the stalled thread holds, so the ~700 MiB store is pinned again through the consumer. "Pending = show no figure" has no mechanism behind it.

(M2) The no-wait guarantee is pinned only on the cancel path. The regex is keyed on a name ("VolumeUsed") that the internal accessor the scanner actually holds is never required to carry.

(M3) The design imported a precondition: drift stays within 64 MiB. The suite's own parallel xUnit classes break it. HardlinkTests writes and deletes exactly 64 MiB, which is the slack, so the Get-Volume bracket test is flaky at validate.

Minor findings:
- The DFS-descent rationale covers only local namespace-server disks. Over SMB, the DFS client chases the referral, which is following a link. The architecture rule makes a DFS exception unwriteable.
- The raw GetDiskFreeSpaceExW drops DriveInfo's media-prompt suppression.
- SUBST and subfolder-mapped drive letters pass IsDriveRoot.
- The TokenElevation helper duplicates Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess.
- VolumeUsed stays pending if the scanner exits before its hook runs.
- The "one source" check in the App is a one-shot name grep.
- The \\?\ invariant is still held by call-site discipline.

Nothing here blocks. Each fix is small and local.

findings.claim:
The design's headline repair is "a read that never returns cannot pin a scan's memory". It holds only inside VolumeSpace.cs.

The stalled thread holds the TaskCompletionSource. The TCS's Task holds every continuation registered on it. The App's consumer is specified only as "takes store.VolumeUsed ... and keeps whatever blocking structure it has now". Whichever form it takes, it references the store or ScanResult on that chain:
- an `await` in an async method with `store` live is a boxed state machine registered on the Task;
- a `.Result` or `.Wait()` on a post-scan thread keeps the store on that thread's stack forever.

Either way, a stalled mapped-drive root scan followed by new scans leaks one whole store per stall, against SL-042's ~136 MiB headroom.

The same sentence also asserts that "a pending figure never blocks the UI thread or the next scan" and that "null and pending both mean no figure is shown". It gives no mechanism for either. If the existing structure is wait-then-ShowOutcome, pending means the outcome and coverage text are never shown, not "no figure". If that thread is a foreground Thread, the process also cannot exit.

Rule 3 (VolumeSpace.cs only) and rule 2 (Core glob only) cover none of this.
findings.evidence: Component 'App outcome reads the scan's figure': "keeps whatever blocking structure it has now, so a pending figure never blocks the UI thread or the next scan"; contract ScanStore.VolumeUsed: "The App waits on its existing post-scan thread and treats null and pending as 'show no figure'"; key_decision "The volume thread captures only the TaskCompletionSource, never the ScanStore"; architecture rule 'the volume read cannot hold a scan's memory' files: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/VolumeSpace.cs only.
findings.fix:
Specify the App shape instead of inheriting it:
- ShowOutcome runs at once without the figure.
- The figure is applied later by a continuation on store.VolumeUsed. That continuation captures only a scan generation number and the window, never the store or ScanResult. It is marshalled to the dispatcher and applied only if the generation still matches.
- Add src/FsAnalyser.App/** to the no-wait rule (no Wait, Result or GetAwaiter on VolumeUsed).
- Add a Core test that makes the no-pin claim behavioural rather than name-based: take a WeakReference to a store, scan a drive root with a blocking reader, register a continuation shaped like the App's, drop the store, GC.Collect, and assert the reference is dead.

To settle it for real: run StallRig against a drive-root scan, rescan twice, and compare private bytes.

findings.claim:
The design calls test 5 "the only thing that pins O-031's reason for existing". Test 5 scans the real C:\ root, so it can only ever end Cancelled. A later wait placed on the normal-completion path passes it. An example is copying the figure into ScanResult at scan end so --report can carry it, which is the natural next change.

The regex backstop is `VolumeUsed\w*\.(Task\.)?(Wait|WaitAsync|GetAwaiter|Result)` plus `await ...VolumeUsed`. The scanner does not hold VolumeUsed. It holds the completion source through "an internal accessor" that the design never names. `_volume.Task.Result`, `source.Task.Wait()` and `Task.WaitAll(t)` all pass the rule. So the guarantee on the path every user takes rests on naming discipline.
findings.evidence: Volume figure tests (5): "a scan of the drive root started with it ends Cancelled while VolumeUsed is still pending"; "Test 5 is the only thing that pins O-031's reason for existing"; case: "Without it, a later .Wait() on the figure passes every other test"; ScanStore component: "An internal accessor hands the completion source" (unnamed); rule 'nothing in Core waits on the volume figure'.
findings.fix: (a) Let the reader run regardless of IsDriveRoot, through an internal overload or a Scanner test parameter. Add a Completed-path twin: scan a small %TEMP% tree to Completed with a blocking reader, and assert that the status is Completed and VolumeUsed is still pending. (b) Either fix the accessor's name in the contract as VolumeUsedSource so the regex matches `.Task.Result` and `.Task.Wait`, or widen the rule over Scanning/** and Store/** to forbid `\.Task\.(Wait|Result|GetAwaiter)\b` on any TaskCompletionSource<long?>.

findings.claim:
The imported precondition is that drift between G1 and G2 is monotone or within 64 MiB. The design's own suite breaks it.

xUnit v2 runs test classes (collections) in parallel by default, and Core.Tests is on xunit 2.9.3. HardlinkTests writes a 64 MiB file and deletes it. If that write lands between G1 and the figure, and the delete lands before G2, the figure sits about 64 MiB plus a few KiB of metadata above max(G1,G2). That is just past the 64 MiB slack, so the test fails. Other worktrees' builds and eng/dotnet.ps1 SDK zip download-then-delete cycles on the same C: are the same shape at larger sizes.

The spike's 30 of 30 inside the bracket was measured with no suite running, so it does not transfer. The result is intermittent red at build and validate on a high-risk slice, with nothing wrong in the code.
findings.evidence: Imported precondition: "Drift in used space during the window is monotone or bounded by the 64 MiB slack. Other processes (TAAD builds, a 300 MB SDK download into .dotnet/) write to the same drive."; Volume figure test (1) bracket [min(G1,G2)-64 MiB, max(G1,G2)+64 MiB]; HardlinkTests "bytes charged once (64 MiB)"; xunit.net: parallelization is "a feature that's enabled by default" (https://xunit.net/docs/running-tests-in-parallel); Stack Overflow answer: "different test classes could run in parallel" (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74863110).
findings.fix:
Put VolumeUsageTests in a `[CollectionDefinition(DisableParallelization = true)]` collection. In xUnit v2 that collection runs alone, after the parallel ones.

Then make test (1) take up to three G1/figure/G2 triples, each with a fresh scan start. It passes if any triple brackets, and on failure it prints every triple.

To check: run the full Core suite about 20 times with the test present, and log the triples.

findings.claim:
The DFS flip is justified with "A descended DFS stub that fails lands in the existing unreadable record, which is never silent." That covers a DFS namespace server's local disk only, where an unhandled tag fails the open. Through SMB it is different: servers present DFS referral points as directories, opening one returns STATUS_PATH_NOT_COVERED, and the client's DFS subsystem chases the referral to the target share. So descending a DFS entry there does not fail. It follows a link into another server, which is exactly what the slice goal ("without ever following a link") forbids.

U-004's reason that descending non-surrogate directories is safe ("all resolved to themselves") was measured on a C: with no DFS in it. Nobody has measured whether a Windows client listing actually carries the DFS tag. If it does not, the flip only matters on namespace-server local disks.

Architecture rule 1 forbids 0x8000000A in EntryClassifier.cs. If a person decides to keep DFS as a link, the rule has to change as well.
findings.evidence: key_decision 1 rationale; coherence_check "descending DFS directories ... no probe on this machine exercised"; U-004 ONLY-UNDER "Non-surrogate directories all resolved to themselves"; samba-technical (Jeff Layton): "CIFS servers generally try to make them look like directories in FIND_FIRST/NEXT responses. When you go to try to do a FIND_FIRST on them though, the server will then (correctly) return STATUS_PATH_NOT_COVERED" (https://lists.samba.org/archive/samba-technical/2013-April/091809.html); MS-CIFS 3.2.5.43: on this error "the client MUST report the error to the DFS subsystem" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-cifs/77604f54-2143-4c20-b51d-9b1c45ae9f3d).
findings.fix: Replace the "never silent" rationale with the true consequence: on a DFS namespace share, descent crosses into target servers, and that is accepted under criterion 4. Or carry the tension between criterion 4 and the goal to a person as a recorded consequence. Do not claim that the unreadable record covers it. Severity is minor because it only bites on enterprise DFS namespaces, not on this person's PC.

findings.claim: Replacing DriveInfo with a raw GetDiskFreeSpaceExW P/Invoke silently drops a guard the BCL applies by construction. DriveInfo wraps its volume calls in DisableMediaInsertionPrompt, which is SetThreadErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS). Without it, a drive-root scan of a removable drive with no media, such as an empty card reader, can raise the system "insert a disk" critical-error dialog from the volume thread.
findings.evidence: key_decision "The source is GetDiskFreeSpaceExW ... It is not DriveInfo". dotnet/runtime DriveInfo.Windows.cs uses `using (DisableMediaInsertionPrompt...` (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem.DriveInfo/src/System/IO/DriveInfo.Windows.cs; the fetched extract shows it on DriveFormat, not the space getters). corefx ac3d3ba moved DriveInfo to SetThreadErrorMode (https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/ac3d3ba). SetThreadErrorMode docs: SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS is used "to prevent error mode dialogs from hanging the application" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/errhandlingapi/nf-errhandlingapi-setthreaderrormode).
findings.fix: Call SetThreadErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS) as the first statement of the dedicated volume thread. Better, put it inside the Native wrapper so no future caller can omit it. If DirectoryReader already guards its opens this way, the guard now lives at two sites held by memory, so move it into one shared helper.

findings.claim: IsDriveRoot is said to keep a whole-volume figure off anything that is not really a drive, because "a mount-point folder or share reporting the whole volume's used space would be a wrong figure with no error". But a SUBST letter (subst S: C:\Users\x) and a letter mapped to a share subfolder are both exactly 'X:\', so they pass. GetDiskFreeSpaceExW then returns the host volume's figure against a tree that covers only a folder. This is pre-existing App behaviour, moved rather than widened, but the IsDriveRoot table claims a protection it does not give.
findings.evidence: key_decision "'Drive root' means what the App already meant: exactly X:\\ after stripping \\\\?\\"; case 'decide whether a root is a drive root' why-text.
findings.fix: Add a SUBST row to the IsDriveRoot table and treat a letter whose QueryDosDevice target begins with \??\ as not a drive root (null). Or record SUBST and subfolder mappings as a known limitation in the case text.

findings.claim: The new TokenElevation.cs P/Invoke helper (OpenProcessToken, GetTokenInformation(20), a 4-byte buffer, Win32Exception) duplicates Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess. That API has been in the BCL since .NET 8, and on Windows it reports token elevation rather than group membership. The dotnet/runtime issue shows it returning true for the UAC-exempt built-in Administrator, which is TokenElevation semantics.
findings.evidence: Component 'Independent-listing long-path test + token helper' -> tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TokenElevation.cs (new). https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/77355 (Implement Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess); https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/84137.
findings.fix: Use `Assert.False(Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess)` and drop the helper file. Confirm once at build that it reads False in testhost; the spike already measured TokenIsElevated=0 there. If the build shows it reads something other than TokenElevation, keep the helper.

findings.claim: The completion source is created in ScanStore's constructor, and only Scanner's start hook completes it. The contract says "never null and completes at most once". It does not say it is always completed, or always has a live read, once the scan method returns. If Scanner throws or returns before reaching VolumeSpace.Start, for example on root normalisation or argument validation, VolumeUsed stays pending forever for a plain folder scan. Any consumer that waits then waits forever.
findings.evidence: ScanStore component: "The Task is created before the scan starts, so it is never null"; Scanner start hook: "At scan start, call VolumeSpace.Start"; contract ScanStore.VolumeUsed.
findings.fix: Add to the contract: when the scan method exits, VolumeUsed is completed or a read thread owns it. Implement it by making Start the scanner's first statement, or with a finally block that calls TrySetResult(null) when Start was not reached. Add one test row: a scan that fails before the hook leaves VolumeUsed completed with null.

findings.claim: "One source, one consumer" is enforced by a one-time build grep that checks VolumeInUse is gone. A later slice that recomputes the figure in the App under any other name, such as a DriveInfo TotalSize minus TotalFreeSpace line in the outcome code, passes. Core's figure then goes unread again, which the design itself calls this project's commonest defect.
findings.evidence: Case 'show the used figure for a drive-root scan in the App': "Build greps that VolumeInUse is gone"; component 'App outcome reads the scan's figure': "DriveInfo stays in the App for the drive list".
findings.fix: Declare a fourth architecture rule, twinned in fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests: src/FsAnalyser.App/** must_not_match `TotalFreeSpace|GetDiskFreeSpace`. Scope it so the drive list's own DriveInfo use still passes, and narrow the pattern if the drive list shows free space.

findings.claim: The long-path no-go is handed to a validate-only case, because testhost is longPathAware and so cannot catch a missing \\?\ prefix. The underlying rule, "every Win32 path Core hands out goes through LongPath.cs", is still discipline at each call site. The design's own new P/Invoke deliberately takes a plain 'X:\' string, and any future plain-string path call site looks the same to every Core test.
findings.evidence: key_decision "No app.manifest / longPathAware in this slice ... The obligation is to scan a >260-character tree through the published exe at validate"; risk spike long-path-testhost-vs-published-exe: no-go, "published exe err 3".
findings.fix: Make the invariant structural: Native path-taking declarations accept the LongPath type rather than string (VolumeSpace's 3-character root can use a named DriveRoot type). Or add longPathAware=true to App.csproj so testhost evidence transfers to the exe. Keep the validate case as confirmation, not as the only guard.

dimensions_checked.result: M3: the imported 64 MiB drift precondition is broken by the suite's own parallel HardlinkTests (64 MiB write then delete). m1: the DFS-descent rationale assumes a failing stub, but SMB DFS referrals are chased by the client. M1: the App's existing blocking structure is assumed to give 'never blocks, pending = no figure' without that being specified. Checked and upheld: the surrogate bit is the N bit per MS-FSCC (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fscc/c8e77b37-3909-4fe6-a4ea-2b9d423b1ee4), the cloud tags and tag 0 are non-surrogate, and the TOKEN_ELEVATION buffer is a 4-byte DWORD.

m3: SUBST and subfolder-mapped letters pass IsDriveRoot and get the host volume's figure. m2: a removable drive with no media raises a media prompt. The rest is covered: tag read only when the attribute is set (EaSize case), hidden entries in the reference listing, drive letter with no volume, folder scan completing null. A per-user quota would make TotalNumberOfBytes quota-limited, but the spike measured no quota and the App had the same exposure, so it is not raised.

M1: the no-pin guarantee is enforced only in VolumeSpace.cs and is re-opened by the App consumer through the TCS continuation chain. M2: the no-wait guarantee is pinned only on the cancel path, and the regex depends on an accessor name the design leaves open.

m4: the TokenElevation P/Invoke helper duplicates Environment.IsPrivilegedProcess. The rest is proportionate to O-031's stall guarantee, which StallRig shows the project already cares about: the VolumeSpace file, the injectable reader, the dedicated thread, three rules and five volume tests.

M1: the pending-figure handling and the store capture in the App are unspecified. m5: VolumeUsed can stay pending forever if the scanner exits before its hook. The classifier contract is total and well defined.

m5: an early scanner exit leaves the Task pending. m2: a critical-error dialog on the volume thread. A false return or exception from GetDiskFreeSpaceExW completing null rather than faulted is correctly specified, and so is a failed descent of a non-surrogate folder going through FolderDone as unreadable.

The O-031 supersession is the design's own LEFT OPEN taste item and is not re-litigated here. It preserves O-031's guarantee and keeps both BCL rules intact. Everything stays inside the recorded stack; powershell.exe 5.1 is used where the spike measured pwsh 7, with a stated fallback. m1 records the tension between criterion 4's DFS descent and the slice goal 'without ever following a link'. Cut criteria 2 and 3 are untouched, and the junction and symlink tags stay surrogate.

M2: the no-wait rule is keyed on a name. m2: the media-prompt guard would be held at call sites instead of in the Native wrapper. m6: 'one source' is a one-shot grep rather than a rule. m7: the \\?\ prefix remains discipline per call site, and the design adds a plain-path P/Invoke. The twin requirement (fitness.yaml plus ArchitectureRulesTests, parity script) is correctly carried.

Criteria 1, 4, 5 and 6 each have a case, and no case serves none. M3: the Get-Volume bracket test is flaky under xUnit's default parallel runs. M2: the stall test covers only a cancelled end, not a Completed one. Criterion 1's independent listing (AttributesToSkip=0, \\?\ root, ordinal set equality, parent-chain rebuild) is a real improvement on the hand-written expected list.

None of consequence. The powershell.exe call in the test uses a fixed command with no interpolated input. The only hardening worth doing is to launch it by absolute path (%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe) rather than a PATH lookup. No elevation is used or needed, and nothing needs to go through the admin operations.
